name: Ski from snowplough to parallel turns
blurb: A week of lessons gets most people down a blue run. The jump from snowplough to parallel is where self-taught skiers stall for years, so it is worth learning properly.
gear: Lessons — genuinely the highest-value purchase in skiing
Boots that fit, which matter far more than skis
steps: Learn the athletic stance: shins pressed against the boot tongues, hands forward and visible, weight centred.
Learn to snowplough, stop, and control speed on a gentle slope.
Learn to turn by steering the legs and rolling the ankles, not by twisting your upper body.
Learn to keep your upper body facing down the hill while your legs turn beneath you.
Move to a stem-christie and then to parallel turns by matching the skis progressively earlier in each turn.
Learn the mountain code: who has right of way, how to stop safely at the side, reading piste markers.
tips: Leaning back is the universal fault and it takes away all your control. Press your shins forward.
Poor-fitting rental boots ruin more ski holidays than bad technique. Get them properly fitted.
proof: You ski a blue run top to bottom in linked parallel turns, in control, and can stop wherever you choose.
